==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|market place|market-place}}

===Etymology===
From {{compound|en|market|place}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|ċēapstōw}}, literally "[[cheap]]-[[stow]]".

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-marketplace.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# An [[open]] [[area]] in a [[town]] housing a [[public]] [[market]].
#: {{syn|en|emporium}}
# The space, actual or metaphorical, in which a [[market]] operates.
#: {{ux|en|Some high-street retailers were slow to enter the new digital '''marketplace''' of the Internet.}}
# {{lb|en|by extension}} The [[world]] of [[commerce]] and [[trade]].
#*: Endorsing the [[liberal]] anti-interventionist credo that the '''marketplace''' should act as the "site of verification," the advocates of [[white lead]] opposed government intervention for the sake of open economic competition, which they claimed revealed its true value and thus should be the sole determinant: "When the railways were built, the [[stage coach]]es disppeared; they died a timely death. If [[zinc white]] is truly superior to [[white lead]], it will kill us in the '''marketplace''', but the government should not intervene." These were the words of {{w|fr:Charles Expert-Bezançon|Expert-Bezançon}}, in his February 1903 deposition to the {{w|National Assembly (France)|parliamentary}} committee examining the bill for banning lead-based pigments in paint.
# {{lb|en|figurative}} A place or sphere for the [[exchange]] of anything, such as ideas or fashions.
#: {{coi|en|{{w|marketplace of ideas|'''marketplace''' of ideas}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=Jason A. Frank; John Tambornino|title=Vocations of Political Theory|page=239
|passage=While political theory frequently appears condemned to nostalgic reflection, cultural studies often dulls its critical edge in the never-ending stampede to document the newest styles and counterstyles of the cultural '''marketplace'''.}}
